status: Research pass for the Media helper. Psychology Today publishes no field limits (its help center is members-only), so limits are the highest length seen on 7 public Chicago profiles, cross-checked with a 2026 third-party report of the live editor. 'limitSource' says which.
notLegalAdvice: The lint rules are a plain-code safety net that is stricter than Illinois law on purpose. They are not legal advice; the clinician stays responsible for what she publishes.

api.note: No public API, partner program or MCP. The help center answers 403 and its API needs a member login.

terms.aiText: AI-written text is allowed only if carefully reviewed, fact-checked and personalized to her own practice; PT may remove text it judges AI-generated or misleading.
terms.noExaggeration: No inaccurate or exaggerated claims about skills, credentials, appointment types, insurance or pricing.
terms.noCopying: No copying from other profiles or sites.

searchCard.note: The card shows the first statement box cut to 4 lines (about 200 to 300 characters, depending on screen width), so the first 200 characters must stand on their own.

directories.name: Google Business Profile
directories.forWho: Public-facing practitioners at a verified location; a solo practitioner with a practice brand uses one profile named '[brand]: [her name]'.
directories.api: Business Profile APIs exist but need approval (verified profile active 60+ days, a website, an application form).
rules: Name must match her real-world name; no keywords, services or city in the name.
Description: no URLs or HTML, no prices or promotions.
directories.difference: One 750-character description built from the first two statement boxes, with no fees in it.

directories.name: GoodTherapy
directories.cost: New Practice Program $25.95 a month or $310 a year (practice 3 years old or less); other tiers not confirmed.
directories.forWho: Individual therapists; license or credentials checked.
directories.difference: Longer bio allowed; GoodTherapy suggests 500-600 words. Join the three statement boxes.

directories.name: Zencare
directories.cost: From $59 a month ($69 in NY and CA) plus $80 setup; includes a photo and video shoot.
directories.difference: Zencare films a short intro video; the statement boxes make a good script outline.

directories.name: TherapyDen
directories.cost: Free profile (not in search results); $30 a month to appear in search.
directories.forWho: Mental health practitioners; needs contact info, About You, issues treated and license info.
directories.difference: 'About You' takes the three statement boxes joined.

directories.name: Open Path Collective
directories.cost: Free for the therapist; the client pays $65 once. She must offer at least one low-fee slot ($40-70 individual, $40-80 couples).
directories.forWho: Licensed or pre-licensed clinicians with an existing practice.
rules: No scheduling or practice links in the profile.
directories.difference: Fees are set by Open Path's sliding scale, not hers; leave the website link out.

directories.name: Headway
directories.cost: Free to join; from November 2026 a $9.99 fee per appointment with a new client found through Headway.
directories.forWho: Clinicians credentialed with insurance through Headway (NPI, CAQH, liability insurance).
directories.difference: Insurance platform: Headway bills insurance, so leave fees and insurance lists out.

directories.name: Alma
directories.forWho: Fully licensed clinicians credentialed under Alma with Aetna, Cigna or Optum.
directories.difference: Insurance platform with consult booking on the profile.

directories.name: Grow Therapy
directories.cost: No membership fee seen; paid per session as a contractor.
directories.forWho: Clinicians with an active unrestricted license and their own malpractice insurance.
directories.difference: Grow's team sets up the profile; she can hand them the statement.

directories.name: Inclusive Therapists
directories.cost: $22 a month billed yearly or $29 monthly; first 90 days free; sliding scale offered.
directories.forWho: Licensed or provisionally licensed clinicians; verification asks about identity, positionality and values.
directories.difference: Identity-focused: she answers their values questions herself.

directories.name: Therapy for Black Girls
directories.forWho: Licensed therapists in private practice; vetted.
directories.difference: Community-focused directory; only list here if it truly fits her practice.

directories.name: Latinx Therapy
directories.cost: $10 or $23 a month, or $223 a year (solo).
directories.forWho: Clinicians committed to cultural humility; every member offers a free consultation.
directories.difference: Needs a free consultation offer; a Spanish listing is on the Standard plan and up.

lintRules.what: Her license designation (for example LCPC) must appear in the profile or site text.
A license title she does not hold, 'Dr.' without a doctorate, or 'board certified'.
A license number (project rule; PT shows the verified number itself).
Stories about a client, case examples.
Promised results: 'guaranteed', 'you will feel better', 'cure', 'in just 6 sessions'.
Rankings that can't be checked: 'best therapist', '#1', 'leading', 'award-winning'.
Anything of value for a review or referral.
Mental health advice or diagnosis: 'you should', 'how to cope', 'signs you have', 'symptoms of'.
Suicide, self-harm or overdose words (the fixed crisis check runs first).
Softer outcome words worth a second look: 'heal', 'overcome', 'find relief'.
'24/7', 'same-day', 'emergency': the practice is not a crisis service.
A fee, insurance plan, free-consult offer, degree or number of years that is not in her saved facts.
Reading grade above 8 or a sentence over 25 words.

default.name: Squarespace Core, paid yearly
default.cost: $29 a month billed yearly ($39 monthly); free domain the first year
default.why: Big template and help library, a 14-day trial with no card, and Core is the cheapest Squarespace plan that lets her paste code (needed for the practice details block for Google).

website.alreadyHasOne: Keep it. Check it against the checklist; add the practice details block only if her site builder allows custom code.

doneForYou.name: Brighter Vision Start
doneForYou.cost: $78 a month billed yearly plus $100 setup

doItYourself.name: A small static site built by a coding agent, on Vercel Pro
doItYourself.why: Vercel Hobby is non-commercial only and GitHub Pages bans running an online business, so a practice site needs a paid host.

meta.note: Meta has no hosted website product. Muse Spark can write page code from a prompt inside Meta AI, with no hosting or domain.

website.hipaa: Show phone and email only, or link to a HIPAA-ready booking tool. Never collect health details in a site's built-in contact form. Squarespace's BAA covers Acuity Scheduling only.

structuredData.note: schema.org has no Psychologist or counselor type; MedicalBusiness is a LocalBusiness subtype. Name and address are required; telephone, url, openingHoursSpecification and priceRange are recommended. No review or aggregateRating.

checklist.label: A clear way to book or ask for a consult on every page
A fees page: session fee, insurance or out-of-network, superbills, the Good Faith Estimate notice for self-pay
The free consult offer (if she has one), said the same way as on Psychology Today
Practice name, address and phone written exactly as on Psychology Today and Google
Her license designation next to her name
No contact form that asks about health or symptoms
A line saying this is not for emergencies: call or text 988, or 911
Readable basics: alt text on photos, real headings, strong contrast, works with a keyboard and zoom
The practice details block for Google pasted in (if the builder allows code)

conversion.evidence: Thin. One study: 44.5% of 238 therapy patients looked up their therapist, mostly online, mainly for professional experience. Industry guides agree on fees up front, a real photo, who she helps, what a first session is like, and how to book.
